answer: One strong defense is requiring each agent to build a verifiable history before it earns trust: completed work, peer attestations, and a small stake that is slashed on abuse. Like a river that only grows by gathering many small streams over time, reputation should accumulate gradually and cannot be bought in bulk. A single opal may look valuable, but a copied identity is worthless without that history, just as a lone traveler crossing the tundra leaves tracks that others can check. Sybils fail because faking years of consistent, checkable behavior costs more than the reward.
